items.stem: A user grants a spending contract an unlimited token allowance. What is the main risk?

options.text: If the contract is buggy or malicious it can move the user's full balance at any time
options.rationale: Correct: unlimited allowance exposes the entire balance indefinitely.

options.text: The user can no longer receive tokens

items.explanation: Correct: unlimited allowance exposes the entire balance indefinitely.

items.stem: Which TWO are reasons to choose a multi-token standard over deploying one fungible-token contract per asset? (Select TWO.)

options.text: A single contract can manage many token types, reducing deployment overhead
options.rationale: Correct: multi-token standards hold many assets in one contract.

options.text: Batch transfers of several token IDs can be done in one transaction
options.rationale: Correct: batching is a core multi-token feature.

options.text: It guarantees the token price will rise
It makes tokens immune to approval risk

items.explanation: Correct: multi-token standards hold many assets in one contract.

items.stem: Why can a fungible token's `decimals` value mislead a developer summing raw balances?

options.text: Raw on-chain balances are integers scaled by decimals, not human-readable amounts
options.rationale: Correct: you must scale by decimals to get display amounts.

options.text: decimals changes the total supply each block
options.rationale: decimals is a fixed display scale.

options.text: decimals is the number of holders
options.rationale: It is not a holder count.

items.explanation: Correct: you must scale by decimals to get display amounts.
